commits: 904f2a2e0d89f495aeb59e49aa716a5abbac4037: docs(agent-seat-hardening): ASH-A Steps 1/2/5/6 — define "main thread", path boundary, agent-type list, SendMessage scope
findings_addressed: Step 1 — dev/design/orchestration.md gains § 1.1 'What "main thread" means' (new, placed after the § 1 anti-patterns, before § 1.5 — no existing section renumbered). States: (a) "main thread" is ROLE-INDEXED, not globally unique — the top-level thread of whatever session is seated in that role; cites the parallel phrasing already in .claude/agents/orchestrator.md and .claude/agents/steward.md; (b) a seat file's `tools:` frontmatter binds ONLY the spawned-subagent case, so a main-thread seat's constraints are a discipline, not a physical guard; (c) counting orchestrators — /orchestrate = orchestrator→implementer = ONE; /steward = steward→orchestrator→implementer = also ONE, because the Steward is explicitly not an orchestrator. Nesting is what the anti-pattern guards (B.1, 2026-05-03; guard = Agent/Task removed from the implementer seat).

Step 1 (chronology, recorded at BOTH sites, anti-patterns SCOPED not deleted) — § 1 anti-pattern bullet and § 10 rule 1 each now carry: dates to 72af7045 (2026-05-17); orchestrator/steward agent types created at 31a73401 (2026-07-02), 46 days later; conclusion 'silent on a Steward-commissioned orchestrator, not prohibitive'; both remain correct about NESTING; both point at § 1.1 for the full argument. Chronology re-verified from git in this worktree (git log -1 --date=short on both SHAs).

Step 2 — new § 1.2 'Write-path boundary by role' in dev/design/orchestration.md is the single authoritative statement: orchestrator/steward MAY write dev/plans/**, dev/design/**, STATUS boards, ledgers, scripts/**; MUST NEVER write src/**, engine/**, or test sources; implementer is the complement (source + tests inside its own worktree; not release plans/boards). Rationale stated plainly: tool-omission is not a guard for a main-thread seat (§ 1.1), and a Bash-holding seat can write any file via `cat >`/heredoc regardless of Edit/Write grants.

Step 2 (cross-reference, prose only) — .claude/agents/orchestrator.md and .claude/agents/steward.md each gained ONE short paragraph naming the path boundary and citing dev/design/orchestration.md § 1.2 as the source of truth (list not restated in three places as a normative copy; the seat paragraphs name it and defer). The `tools:` frontmatter lines in BOTH files are byte-identical to baseline — verified: `git diff -- .claude/agents/ | grep -E '^[-+]tools:'` returns nothing.

Step 5 — AGENTS.md § 7 valid-`subagent_type` list updated: added `orchestrator`; added `steward` explicitly annotated '**main-thread-only — do NOT spawn**' with the reason (a spawned steward structurally cannot be the propose-first interface to the HITL: it has no channel to the human, its output returns to its spawner). All prior entries kept; 'Never guess or invent a type' kept verbatim; added the snapshot warning naming that the list has gone stale TWICE (written at b52b50c3, 2026-06-28, four days before orchestrator/steward existed at 31a73401, 2026-07-02) and must be re-checked against .claude/agents/ when a type is added.

Step 6 — dev/design/orchestration.md § 6 fresh-spawn paragraph SCOPED, not overturned: its reasoning is preserved and explicitly extended to fix-N and to every hand-off across a subagent boundary that has ALREADY CLOSED (on-disk state is the contract; a warm resident is never a substitute for the artifact). SendMessage is scoped to the one case on-disk state cannot serve — correcting or halting a still-running subagent — and never replaces the brief, the output.json, or the codex § 9 gate. Recorded caveat: whether a mid-flight steer counts against the § 6 fix-N round cap is OPEN and UNRULED (HITL) — the breaker counts ROUNDS (a round = a discrete briefed spawn), a steer is not a round, so drip-fed corrections inside one round would never trip the cap; until ruled, the seats are NOT granted SendMessage and the paragraph states intent, not a currently-available capability.

No tracked file was 'fixed' on anyone's behalf. After the symlink, agent-lint-md.sh rc=0 at baseline, establishing a clean 5/5 baseline before my first edit.

additional_changes_made_in_scope: AGENTS.md § 7 line 88 ('Main thread orchestrates. Do not spawn an "orchestrator" subagent…') was scoped with one clause, NOT deleted: it now reads 'from inside an orchestrator or an implementer — no nesting; the main thread of a session IS that session's orchestrator', plus a pointer to dev/design/orchestration.md § 1.1 for the definition and chronology. Reason: Step 1 scopes the identically-worded orchestration.md § 1 / § 10 lines, and leaving AGENTS.md § 7 stating the unscoped form would leave the repo self-contradicting on exactly the point this slice exists to settle. AGENTS.md is on the MAY-edit list; the change is one bullet, additive, and states no new rule.

No other file touched.
